subject: Re: Unitization policy — carryover credits & prefix allocation
messages:
From: Liz Chen <liz@novahealth.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: Tom Baker <tbaker@novaplatforms.com>
Date: 2028-06-01T09:04:00-07:00
Subject: Unitization questions: carryover & prefix allocation

Hi Karthik,

Quick follow-up from our finance team after the commercial call — two specific things they want written confirmation on before we sign: 1) how do unused 'unitization credits' (carryover) behave when a customer oscillates between high and low consumption months; and 2) how prefix/KV cache reuse is accounted for across sessions when a single user maintains a long-running conversation vs. many short chats.

Examples they asked for: if NovaHealth hits committed units in May (bursty) and then is at 20% of commit in June, do unused micro-credits roll forward, or are they considered consumed by the highest-window buckets? Also, from an implementation standpoint, when we warm KV cache for a long patient chat thread, is that warming charged as tokens once per model warmup, or repeatedly per session slice?

We want to make sure the contract language aligns with what you actually bill. If you can send a short worked example and a one-paragraph contract-friendly summary that the legal/procurement team can accept, we can move contract redlines to signature.

Attachment: I attached the current redlined contract (nova-contract-redlines.pdf).

Thanks,
Liz
Liz Chen
Head of Integrations, NovaHealth

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: Liz Chen <liz@novahealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Date: 2028-06-01T12:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Unitization questions: carryover & prefix allocation

Hi Liz — thanks for the clear asks. Short answers up front, then a worked example and a contract-friendly clause you can paste into procurement.

Short answers:
- Carryover: We do not "roll" unused committed credits indefinitely. We provide a 90-day carryover window that can be applied to shortfalls in later months; after 90 days, remaining committed credits expire.
- Prefix/KV warming: We bill warming (the tokens used to populate KV/prefix state) at the time of the first request that triggers the warm. If that same client reuses the cache (within the same active conversation ID and within our active-ttl window), subsequent requests that hit the warmed KV do not incur the same warmup token charge. However, separate conversation IDs or TTL expiry will re-trigger warmup and the warming tokens will be billed again.

Worked example (simplified):
- Commit: 1,000,000 units/month (unit = 1,000 token quantum for accounting).
- May: actual usage = 1,300,000 tokens (1.3M) -> consumes 1,300 units. Commit covers 1,000 units; 300 units draw from overage or from committed burst buffer.
- June: actual usage = 200,000 tokens -> 200 units. We allow up to 90 days for unused commit credits to be applied. In this case, because May exceeded commit, there are no unused credits to carry forward. For a month where actual < commit, the delta (commit - actual) becomes carryover credit for up to 90 days.

KV/prefix billing example:
- Conversation A: initial prompt sequence (1,200 tokens) warms KV cache and is billed as 2 units (rounded up to our 1,000-token quantum).
- Subsequent turns in Conversation A within 48h TTL that reuse the same KV hits will not be billed again for that warmup portion; only new generated tokens are billed.
- Conversation B (different convo id) that needs the same KV state will behave as a cold start and warming tokens will be billed again.

Rounding/minimums note:
- We bill in fixed quanta (1,000-token unit). Usage is aggregated per-customer per-month and rounded up to the nearest quantum for invoicing. We do not prorate down. This is the simplest deterministic approach for invoicing and aligns with how we present usage on the invoice.

Contract phrasing you can use: "Redwood will apply committed unit carryover for shortfalls for up to 90 days following the month of the commit. Warming or prefix-populate tokens incurred to initialize a conversation-level KV cache are billed on first occurrence per conversation ID and within the active KV TTL; subsequent requests that hit the warmed KV do not re-bill the warmup tokens. Tokens are invoiced in 1,000-token quanta and usage is aggregated monthly and rounded up to the next quantum."

Attachment: I looked at nova-contract-redlines.pdf and added a few inline comments (will send separately to marissa for commercial sign-off).

If you'd like a diagram or a one-page math example tailored to your average conversation length, tell me your 95th percentile conversation token length and I can sketch it.

Best,
Karthik
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: Liz Chen <liz@novahealth.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Date: 2028-06-02T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Unitization questions: carryover & prefix allocation

Hi Liz — looping in Vanessa from pricing. Appreciate the prompt. Two practical commercial options we can offer so procurement has clarity:

Option A — Standard commit + 90d carryover (no change): commitments apply monthly, up to 90-day carryover, invoiced in 1k-token units.

Option B — Predictable smoothing pilot (3 months): we set a smoothing bucket that allows NovaHealth to draw down a rolling micro-credit pool for +/-30% variance month-to-month before hitting overage. Pilot terms: 3-month pilot, 10% discount on overage rate, and a single contract addendum documenting the smoothing bucket. This is intended for customers with predictable seasonal variance and avoids frequent monthly true-ups.

For KV/prefix concerns, we can include a single-line SLA: if NovaHealth supplies a canonical conversation id and maintains it through the session for externally-provided context, Redwood will consider warming charged once per conversation id per TTL period. We'll mark TTL as 48h standard and allow negotiation to 72h for enterprise customers.

If you're leaning Option B, we can draft the addendum and include a short clause for legal. If standard commit is acceptable, we will proceed to finalize redlines with the existing 90-day carryover language that Karthik pasted.

Marissa Cole
Head of Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference
Attachment: pricing-smoothing-proposal.pdf (sent via Drive link)

From: Liz Chen <liz@novahealth.com>

Subject: Re: Unitization questions: carryover & prefix allocation

Thanks Karthik and Marissa — this is very helpful. NovaHealth prefers Option B for the initial twelve-month relationship and the 3-month smoothing pilot makes procurement comfortable. Two asks before signature: 1) please add the TTL language (48h default, 72h negotiable) into the addendum, and 2) include an explicit example in the addendum showing how the smoothing pool would be consumed when May is +40% and June is -25% relative to commit.

We'll accept the 10% pilot overage discount and want the addendum to be attached to the main SOW. Please send a draft addendum and we'll loop legal for a final pass.

I also attached a small kv-warmup-sample.log that shows our client behavior so you can confirm the TTL assumption is compatible with our usage patterns.

Best,
Liz
Head of Integrations, NovaHealth
